## 0. How to read this document

This file is the single source of truth for Gripfactory Lite. If a chat, a file, or a piece of code disagrees with this file, **this file wins** until it is amended through the Loop.

1. **Nothing is canon until it appears in this file.** Verbal agreements and prior chats do not count.
2. **Names listed here are exact:** no casing changes, no synonyms, no close enough.
3. **No drive-by edits.** Changes land through the Loop: decide, ratify, fold, version bump.

---

## 1. Identity

**Gripfactory Lite** (working title; repo folder "gripfactory Practical") is a lite rebuild of Gripfactory: the **opsHelpers database architecture** as the base, the **end state of Gripfactory as the design compass**, the **harvest console** incorporated. One job: **run harvest and post-harvest operations without interruptions.**

"C-Drive based" means the **repo lives on Dennis's disk**, outside corporate git (clarified 2026-08-27). The product itself is hosted.

It is also the **upstream canon for the node consoles.** Compliance Console canon already names "gripFactory canon, upstream and read-only" as its base: nodes may extend upstream canon and may never contradict it.

One codebase, two Cloudflare deployments, same behavior, different CSS tokens, each storing its own data on-site:

- **Grip internal site**: runs the actual 2026 harvest at Grip. Recipient: **Corey**.
- **C10 site**: the standalone product on The Continuum 10. Recipient: **Christine**.

## 1b. Terms (owner cleanup, 2026-08-31, verbatim where quoted)

- **HBN**: "a METRC name for a harvest, no matter what parent packages come and go, this HBN follows every subsequent package around." The HBN is the METRC harvest NAME; it rides the HarvestName column of METRC uploads and names upload files.
- **Lot**: "The year and sequential order of the harvest YY###."
- **Package ID**: "METRC Package ID, can refer to all of or parts of a lot."
- Lifecycle: "Early in life, product is managed by lot. As the lots get broken down, the lot number matters less and less. But at the end of everything when you're reviewing the data, the HBN is the only thing that ties a FG to harvest batch."
- Known tension, unruled: the app's operator surfaces say "Start lot / Finish lot" for wet_weight_entries rows (one per destination within an HBN), while the canonical Lot is the YY### itself. Renaming those surfaces awaits an owner ruling.

## 2. Success criteria

1. The Grip harvest runs on it from **2026-09-01** without interruption.
2. A **hosting package** ships to both recipients: a **zip of the repo plus a README addressed to the recipient's Claude agent**, which deploys it to that recipient's Cloudflare (Corey: Grip internal; Christine: C10). (The Harvest Console `handoff/` pattern is the proven precedent.)
3. Related hard date: the C10 Compliance Console surface has a hard need of **2026-09-09** (its own canon, §2).

## 4. Standing rules (guardrails)

- **G-1, One remote, GitHub, private; a push is a conversation (amended 2026-09-24, canon 0.30.223; amended again 2026-09-27, canon 0.30.261; owner: "I want to allow the scribe to push.  It just needs to be a conversation each pass.").** The repo on Dennis's disk is the working tree and the source of truth; it has one remote, a private GitHub repository under his account or the OCG organization. A push is his hands by default: the Scribe hands the block and he runs it (his stated preference). The Scribe may push only by his word in the conversation for that one push, given after the Scribe has said what the push carries (the files, the commit message, the branch); a yes covers one push and is never carried forward, never taken from a fold, a gate, a schedule or the road lane's request file, and never inferred. The Scribe never adds a remote, never force-pushes, never rewrites history, never pushes a branch he has not named, and never holds a credential in chat, canon, a report or a log (a credential the Scribe's shell uses sits in a file git reads by itself, ignored by git, scoped to this repository, his to mint and revoke). A build session never runs git on the tree at all. `main` mirrors the disk until the deploy from the push lands (the plan of 0.30.260); branches are built on his disk and pushed when they are ready to merge. DROPS/, db_backups/, DEPLOY/, _to_delete/ and RESEARCH/ never ride (.gitignore). Before this amendment: pushed by his hands alone, the Scribe never pushes (2026-09-24); no GitHub, no pushes, no remotes (2026-08-27).
- **G-2, Build lanes (amended 2026-08-27: "the bones all seem to work").** The Scribe may apply small slices directly from its session; Cursor remains the lane for large or structural work. Either lane owes the same discipline: sealed final check, session report, migrations frozen post-deploy.
- **G-3, No flubdubs.** No speculative features, invented fields, or decorative complexity. The screens fill with real operations; lean beats clever. (Dennis, 2026-08-27)
- **G-4, Repo on disk, app in the cloud (amended 2026-08-27).** The repo lives on Dennis's disk, never corporate git. The app runs as two Cloudflare sites (Grip internal, C10): same code and behavior, different CSS tokens, each storing its own data on-site. SQL stays Postgres-portable for the possible future Plato-on-Aurora integration.
- **G-5, opsHelpers is the db base**, defined as Plato Bible §4 standing rules, §5 naming conventions, and §6 canonical schema: snake_case English identifiers, grams canonical, UTC storage, audit columns on every row, soft delete plus edit-with-reason into `record_change_log`, lookup-table enums, configurable utilities as data not code, repository-layer storage abstraction. The Plato governance apparatus is **not** carried.
- **G-6, Canon home and mirror.** `canon/` in the repo is the canonical home; the Claude Project holds the Scribe's synced mirror. Every fold updates both. Repo home ratified at `Documents\Claude\Projects\gripfactory Practical` (2026-08-27).
- **G-7, The Box Doctrine is the build law.** See §5.
- **G-8, Style law: no em dashes or en dashes anywhere**: chat, documents, UI strings, code comments, generated files. Commas, colons, semicolons, periods, or a plain spaced hyphen instead. (Owner directive, global, 2026-08-11.)
- **G-9, Ship clean.** Shipped packages carry no personnel or internal-meeting content. (Harvest Console v0.94 scrub is precedent; crew names in working data stay internal.)
- **G-10, Build verification.** Every Cursor prompt requires a session report plus the sealed final check: byte size, sha256, parse test, and tail inspection for every touched file, output pasted verbatim into the report.

## 5. The Box Doctrine (ratified 2026-08-27)

The unit of build is **the box**. The harvest process map (Dennis's Visio, transcribed in `canon/PROCESS_MAP.md`, image at `canon/harvest-process-map.png`) is the territory. **The map is walked in order.**

**The Box Contract**, all three or it is not done:

1. A **worker** can perform the process.
2. A **manager** can audit it.
3. A **report or CSV** comes out of it.

The working method per box:

1. Dennis supplies the current tool: the OpsHelpers equivalent or the spreadsheet the box runs on today.
2. The Scribe and Dennis **talk the box through before any design.** No designing ahead of the current box.
3. Then spec, then Cursor builds, then verification, then the box is adopted and the walk moves on.

**Standing duty:** the Scribe holds the map and reminds Dennis when work drifts off the current box. The Scribe polices itself the same way: design sprawl is drift.

## 6. Architecture and key decisions

- **ADR-1 (2026-08-27):** opsHelpers db architecture per G-5 is the foundation. Proven in operation; a 5-day runway forbids novel architecture.
- **ADR-2 (2026-08-27, amended same day):** **TypeScript** backbone per the cross-project standard (Dennis 2026-07-22; SalesHelper canon §2). Store of record on Cloudflare is **D1**: a documented exception to the Postgres law, accepted by owner delegation (2026-08-27: limited resources, no appetite for another server). All SQL is written ANSI-portable so a Postgres/Aurora port is a dialect change, not a rewrite. PGlite remains the option for a future local edition.
- **ADR-3 (2026-08-27):** Gripfactory end state is the design compass; the harvest console is incorporated, not reinvented. The new-farm edition is the live console lineage (promoted 2026-08-06); the exact incorporation shape gets decided when the walk reaches console-shaped boxes.
- **ADR-4 (2026-08-27):** Single-file static deliverables for the C10 host contract (one self-contained HTML file, no server, no network calls) apply to console-type nodes hosted on the existing C10 static path; the Gripfactory Lite app itself deploys per ADR-5.
- **ADR-5 (2026-08-27):** **The queue spine.** The build follows Dennis's nine-step chain (Acquire HBN → HBN Queue → Wet Weight Entry → Dry Space Queue → Trim Packages Entry → Cryo Queue → Cryo Weight Entry → Testing Queue → manual testing-queue controls) as simple forms on **Cloudflare Workers + D1**, two wrangler environments (grip, c10), stations and queues defined in one typed registry so pipeline order is data and new stations insert without rework. HBN date segment: **YYDDD Julian** (owner ruling 2026-08-27), replacing the 25H Excel serial.
- **ADR-6 (2026-08-27):** **The mint law, corrected against the 25H formula and owner ruling.** `<YYDDD>-<farm>-<grow_code>-<strain_code>-<manicure>-<silo>-<YY###>`. The trailing segment is **YY + a 3-digit year-wide lot serial** in mint order (26001, 26002, ...), resetting each year: the floor's primary identifier and the largest number on the traveler. Numeric silo numbers render 2-digit zero-padded (5 → 05); blank → NA. Serials are never reused; voids leave auditable gaps.

- **ADR-7 (2026-08-31): The auth surface.** Three layers, all live. (1) **Cloudflare Access** walls the whole site: Zero Trust org gflite, One-time PIN login, emails ending @gripcannabis.com. (2) **Identity is the Access login email** (owner ruling: "Replace the Person selector with the cloudflare email address used at login"): a middleware reads Cf-Access-Authenticated-User-Email, people rows auto-create on first login (unique email column, display name from the local part, editable in Lookups), the actor for every write is the login person and is never trusted from the form. The wet weight **Lead stays a picker** (owner ratification) and stores on the lot as lead_person_id. Local dev and smoke run without Access and act as dev@local. Access-JWT verification (AUD tag) is parked hardening. (3) **PIN gate** (owner ruling: "Gate Admin and Interco logistics with a PIN prompt, 21319 is the only valid PIN"): /admin, /admin/*, and /interco demand the PIN, which lives as data in app_config (L-4), one unlock holds per device for 12 hours via cookie. Amended 2026-08-31: /fulfillment and /fulfillment/* sit behind the same gate (the Fulfillment tile, folded at 0.7.1).

- **ADR-8 (2026-08-31): The two-pane station theme is law.** Owner, verbatim: "left pane: available-in-queue, right pane: what's currently saved about that record and the ability to add more to it"; extended by owner ruling to everything ("It will extend to everything"). Every station renders its feeding queue as the left pane and the picked record's saved state plus its add controls as the right pane; record views (the wet lot ledger, the unload dry ledger) render as right-pane panels on the two-pane page, never as standalone pages. Acquire HBN is the source station with no feeding queue and keeps its plain form: the sole standing exception until the owner says otherwise.

**Reference map** (read-only sources, sibling folders): `gripfactory/PLATO_BIBLE.md` (the opsHelpers schema and rules) · `gripfactory/SCRIBE_NOTES_V4.md` (verification discipline, failure patterns) · `Harvest Console/harvest-console-CANON.md` and `Harvest Console/new-farm/NEW-FARM-CANON.md` (console lineage) · `Harvest Console/handoff/HOSTING.md` (hosting package precedent) · `SalesHelper/CANON.md` (stack law, style law) · `Compliance Console/ComplianceConsole_CANON.md` (node contract, C10/GF split).

## 7. Lessons register (the compass, ratified 2026-08-27)

- **L-1** Ceremony dies, schema survives. Plato's Tier 3 governance was retired within weeks; its schema and naming rules outlived everything. Govern light, keep the schema strict.
- **L-2** Cloud lanes go dormant, offline-first wins. v4_v2 on Cloudflare stalled; the single-file offline console shipped and got hosted. (History stands; the 2026-08-27 hosting ruling reverses course deliberately, hedged by the zip + README package and Postgres-portable SQL.)
- **L-3** The proven build loop: Scribe writes the spec, Cursor builds, headless verification, owner sees it working. Honor it per box.
- **L-4** Values live in data, not code. The 448 g/lb buried-formula lesson (Plato §4.10): any raw-to-displayed transformation is user-editable configuration.
- **L-5** Truncation is real. Every write gets the sealed final check; mount views can lie; sha256 from both sides settles it.
- **L-6** OneDrive and folder mounts bite: a live .git will not run on the mounted folders from the Scribe's side; Cursor's native git is fine; repos travel as zips.

R2/R3: the Start time takes the app's HH:MM colon mask (data-time24-mask, the Acquire idiom); THE LOADED TIME IS THE CLOCK'S ZERO: the typed Start time (resolved in the browser's local day; blank = now) becomes loaded_at and the clock runs from it the moment the silo loads; the load view shows Loaded (rendered local) and the clock; Start stays as ruled and is greyed from the load; Pause/Resume and the Pencil (editing loaded_at, the zero) unchanged. THE LAW: the drop page sends the file in rounds of 5,000 rows (METRC_SLICE_ROWS), each round its own request (slice, slice_size, mount_id), each answering JSON, refusals in JSON words; the file streams once per round (every row read so the tags seen and the summary total the whole file; only the window's rows shaped, diffed by tag against the mirror, and written); round zero writes the mount row with the file's row count and a summary reading mounting with rows done; every round adds its counts to the mount row in the same final batch as its rows; the last round marks gone (the mirror's live tags under the license, and the phase for plants, minus every tag the file carries), writes the real summary and logs the final counts; a later round is checked against its mount (kind, license, phase, row count) or refused; a mount whose rounds never finished reads unfinished, N of total rows in the Mounts table; the line under the button counts the rounds; a browser without the script posts once and the Worker walks the file in one request as before. THE MIRROR LAW ACROSS OUR OWN LICENSES (a fault found on the way): the window's existing rows are read by tag alone, so a package the mirror holds under one license, dropped in another license's file, updates in place, license included, where the 0.30.38 mount would have collided on the tag. | 0.30.92 | 2026-09-16 | THE EFFECTIVE DATE (Scribe-direct under G-2). Two owner rulings 2026-09-16, minutes apart, verbatim: "We need to quickly add a date override in the load silo screen - PIN gated: 21319  Correcting for the issues from yesterday has made it impossible for me to load the silos at their proper time because the default date is today." and "Next move "Effective Date" = field on all transactional records - always pin gated - defaults to today and rarely needs to be touched." THE LAW: Effective Date is a field on a transactional record's form. It defaults to today (the farm's day, Eastern) and rarely needs to be touched: collapsed, one line reading Effective Date: YYYY-MM-DD (today). Opened, it offers the date (capped at today) and an Admin PIN box; any day other than today is honored only with the Admin PIN (app_config admin_pin) typed beside it, never a day ahead of today; blank, absent or today asks no PIN. The record's own instant falls on that day. Every write under another day leaves a change-log row with the reason effective date set under the Admin PIN (SYSTEM_REASON.effective_date), so the override is never silent. One field, one law: names effective_date and effective_pin, helper effectiveDateField and resolveEffectiveDate in src/effective.ts, the farm's clock in src/farmday.ts (etDate, etInstant, isCalendarDate, the console's helpers moved there and re-exported). | 0.30.96 | 2026-09-16 | THE PENDING QUEUE CLEAR (Scribe-direct under G-2). Owner ruling 2026-09-16, verbatim: "CAN WE REMOVE ALL THE DOCS that are parked on pending data uploads?" His picks (AskUserQuestion): the clear records the files as cleared, NOT uploaded to METRC (an honest disposition, never a false upload claim), and it is a reusable Clear all button on the page, not a one-time SQL. THE PICTURE: the queue was the whole harvest so far because nothing had ever been marked uploaded (metrc_uploads held two package_adjust marks); every finished batch, silo load, manifest and receipt pended. THE LAW: a Clear all pending control at the top of Pending Data Uploads, revealed behind a summary so a stray click cannot fire it, carrying the total across all seven lists (the whole /admin tree is behind the Admin PIN, so the clear is PIN-gated by that gate); one post disposes every pending file across the seven lists (wet weights, package files, receive manifests, manifests, splits, location changes, location moves) by inserting one metrc_uploads row per file with cleared = 1 and the change-log reason 'cleared, not uploaded to METRC', so the disposition is honest and never recorded as a METRC upload. It reuses the existing disposition path (the pending predicates already read any metrc_uploads row of a file's kind and ref as disposing it), so NO pending query changed; a future 'uploaded to METRC' report filters cleared = 0. No CSV is built (the bounded Worker room, 0.30.42): a cleared row needs only the kind, the batch and the ref the pending lists already carry, its filename a plain cleared_<kind>_<name>.csv. Reversibility matches per-item Mark uploaded: a time-based kind (wet weights, splits) re-pends on new activity, an existence kind stays cleared until its row is voided; the underlying harvest data is untouched, only clear-marks written. BUILT: migration 0054 (cleared column on metrc_uploads, default 0 so every existing mark stays a real upload), src/config.ts (SYSTEM_REASON.upload_cleared), src/actions.ts (clearAllUploads gathers the seven pending lists and inserts a cleared row per file, one db.batch), src/index.ts (POST /admin/uploads/clear-all, the ok=cleared flash), src/html.ts (the Clear all reveal and button with the total), src/i18n.ts EN and ES; test/surface.test.ts (the control renders with the summed count, none when empty); the smoke's clear-all walk (the from-zero pin is 54; with a pile pending the button carries a count, one post disposes every kind, the page reads Nothing pending, the flash says not-uploaded, the change log carries the reason). The Scribe's answer: the Worker keeps every instant in UTC and has no zone of its own; every screen converts to the browser's zone for display and every typed floor time (the Start time on Load Silo, the Effective Date) converts server-side in the farm's zone, Eastern, so a mis-set tablet cannot skew a record; the silo load pencil was the one field left taking the raw stored form and saving what was typed, unchecked. With the old box the only fix was to type the UTC clock four hours ahead with the Z, the date rolling after 8 PM Eastern, which is the trap itself, so the pencil was rebuilt instead. THE LAW AS BUILT (Scribe-direct under G-2): a stored instant a pencil takes is a FARM-TIME field (EditFieldDef.farmTime); it shows the stored instant as the Eastern wall clock (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM) and takes the same shape back; the server parses it through farmInstantFromInput in src/farmday.ts (a zoneless wall clock is Eastern and resolves through etInstant, a space or a T between and seconds ignored; an instant carrying its zone, Z or an offset, stands as it is; any other shape refuses in words, Loaded at must be a farm-time date and time, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM.; a blank refuses, Loaded at is required.; more than ten minutes ahead of now refuses, Loaded at is ahead of now.); nothing zoneless is ever stored again; old and new instants log under the typed reason. The silo load pencil is the first farm-time field, labeled Loaded at (farm time, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, the clock's zero); a zoneless value already stored shows in the box as the wall clock of the instant the Worker actually runs the clock from, so the box tells the truth about the zero. etWallClock(iso) renders any instant as the Eastern wall clock. The Load Silo form was never wrong (resolveLoadedAt and etInstant already stored the instant with its Z). HIS PICKS on the question tool: the weight of a parent package is "The batch weight at its first full panel" (the order's batch_grams; offered: the parent's live METRC weight; the lot's dry weight); the denominator is "Every representative package with a full-panel result" (a first fail counts as not once from that moment, whether or not the retest has happened; pending panels, potency-only and R&D orders stay out; offered: only packages at a final pass; every package ever scheduled); the lane is "Deploy part 2 now, fix the rate as part 2b before part 3" (offered: hold the deploy; Scribe-direct). THE FIRST FULL PANEL: a parent enters the rate when its earliest panel = full_compliance order has a sample with overall_passed set; passed means it needed one panel, failed means it did not, from that moment, whatever a retest or a remediation does later; potency and rnd orders are never a panel for this rate; a parent with no resulted full panel is not in it. THE WEIGHT is that first order's batch_grams; THE RATE is the weight of the parents that needed one panel over the weight of every parent in the rate, shown to one decimal with the pounds (at 448, two decimals) and the package counts under it; an empty season reads no results. BY LAB (the lab of the first full panel) then FAILURE TYPE (the failed test types of that panel, by weight and count, a two-type fail under both); BY STRAIN (the HBN's) then FARM; the COA and THC lists stay keyed on the parent tag and gain the attempt beside the date. THE LAW: (1) THE DRYING TOTALS, one line under the dry space tiles in the console's Drying section (/harvest), three figures, each the pounds at 448 and the whole grams with the lot count under. Total in Dry Spaces is the wet weight of the open loads in the silos and the dry rooms only (the freezer's chilling material and the lots still waiting to load stay out), and under it the dry estimate, est. dry X lb at P percent, the loaded grams times the Admin percent (app_config projected_dry_yield_pct, the same number the tiles' of expected reads; 22 by default and 22 on his floor since 0.30.77; his default to 21 is the number to set there, so the two surfaces never disagree). Total in Cure Spaces is the dry weight of the lots on CSA and CSB. Total Dry Queued is the Unloaded Queue for trim (unloaded lots with a live trim schedule, the queue the trimming clocks read), its dry grams. Owner, 2026-09-23, verbatim: "I'm not sure the production scheduling surface for prepack makes sense to me.  If I adopt a package to an HBN does it conflate that package ID to the HBN I adopted? A filter at the top of the list for HBN or last 6 would be useful, but the scheduler should only really be scheduling by the package ID (or the last six digits of it).  Use the ">>"/"<<" system we've precedented throughout the app." THE SCRIBE'S ANSWER: today's Adopt writes the picked HBN onto the package (its lot, its ledger item, its schedule row), a binding and not a filter; and the prepack Available pane's >> inherited the trim pattern, scheduling every passed WPR of an HBN at once (scheduleHbn). Both go.
